name.text: Estimating an area by counting squares

questiontext.text:
The plan shows [[if test="is(cc=0)"]]a fish pond on a farm in Kirinyaga[[elif test="is(cc=1)"]]a patch of papyrus swamp near Kisumu[[else]]a rocky outcrop in a field near Machakos[[/if]] drawn on a grid. Each square stands for \({@s@}\,\text{m}\) by \({@s@}\,\text{m}\).

[[jsxgraph width="480px" height="360px"]] (function() { var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [-0.3, 9.3, 12.3, -0.3], axis: false, grid: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}}); function blobPoly(cx, cy, R, a, bb, ph) { var p = [], K = 1440, k, t, r; for (k = 0; k < K; k++) { t = 2 * Math.PI * k / K; r = R * (1 + a * Math.cos(2 * (t - ph)) + bb * Math.cos(3 * t)); p.push([cx + r * Math.cos(t), cy + r * Math.sin(t)]); } return p; } var poly = blobPoly({#cx#}, {#cy#}, {#Rr#}, {#aa#}, {#bb#}, {#ph#}); for (var g = 0; g <= 12; g++) { b.create('segment', [[g, 0], [g, 9]], {strokeColor: '#999999', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } for (var h = 0; h <= 9; h++) { b.create('segment', [[0, h], [12, h]], {strokeColor: '#999999', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } var X = [], Y = []; for (var k = 0; k <= poly.length; k++) { X.push(poly[k % poly.length][0]); Y.push(poly[k % poly.length][1]); } b.create('curve', [X, Y], {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 2, fillColor: '#cccccc', fillOpacity: 0.45, fixed: true, highlight: false}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

A full square lies wholly inside the shape. A part square has the edge passing through it.

(a) How many full squares are there?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

(b) How many part squares are there?

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(c) Estimate the area of the shape in squares.

[[input:ans3]] squares [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt2]]

(d) Estimate the area of the shape in square metres.

[[input:ans4]] \(\text{m}^2\) [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:
[[jsxgraph width="480px" height="360px"]] (function() { var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [-0.3, 9.3, 12.3, -0.3], axis: false, grid: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}}); function blobPoly(cx, cy, R, a, bb, ph) { var p = [], K = 1440, k, t, r; for (k = 0; k < K; k++) { t = 2 * Math.PI * k / K; r = R * (1 + a * Math.cos(2 * (t - ph)) + bb * Math.cos(3 * t)); p.push([cx + r * Math.cos(t), cy + r * Math.sin(t)]); } return p; } function clipFrac(poly, x0, y0) { var p = poly, e, i, P, Q, out, ax, v, ge, t, inP, inQ, A = 0; var edges = [[0, x0, 1], [0, x0 + 1, 0], [1, y0, 1], [1, y0 + 1, 0]]; for (e = 0; e < 4; e++) { ax = edges[e][0]; v = edges[e][1]; ge = edges[e][2]; out = []; if (p.length === 0) { break; } for (i = 0; i < p.length; i++) { P = p[(i + p.length - 1) % p.length]; Q = p[i]; inQ = ge ? Q[ax] >= v : Q[ax] <= v; inP = ge ? P[ax] >= v : P[ax] <= v; if (inQ) { if (!inP) { t = (v - P[ax]) / (Q[ax] - P[ax]); out.push([P[0] + t * (Q[0] - P[0]), P[1] + t * (Q[1] - P[1])]); } out.push(Q); } else if (inP) { t = (v - P[ax]) / (Q[ax] - P[ax]); out.push([P[0] + t * (Q[0] - P[0]), P[1] + t * (Q[1] - P[1])]); } } p = out; } for (i = 0; i < p.length; i++) { P = p[(i + p.length - 1) % p.length]; Q = p[i]; A += P[0] * Q[1] - Q[0] * P[1]; } return Math.abs(A) / 2; } function shade(b, sq) { for (var q = 0; q < sq.length; q++) { var i = sq[q][0], j = sq[q][1]; b.create('polygon', [[i, j], [i + 1, j], [i + 1, j + 1], [i, j + 1]], {fillColor: '#777777', fillOpacity: 0.55, borders: {strokeWidth: 0}, vertices: {visible: false}, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } } function hatch(b, sq) { var X = [], Y = []; for (var q = 0; q < sq.length; q++) { var i = sq[q][0], j = sq[q][1]; X.push(i, i + 0.5, NaN, i, i + 1, NaN, i + 0.5, i + 1, NaN); Y.push(j + 0.5, j, NaN, j + 1, j, NaN, j + 1, j + 0.5, NaN); } b.create('curve', [X, Y], {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } var poly = blobPoly({#cx#}, {#cy#}, {#Rr#}, {#aa#}, {#bb#}, {#ph#}); var full = [], part = [], i, j, fr; for (i = 0; i < 12; i++) { for (j = 0; j < 9; j++) { fr = clipFrac(poly, i, j); if (fr > 0.99999) { full.push([i, j]); } else if (fr > 1e-9) { part.push([i, j]); } } } shade(b, full); hatch(b, part); for (var g = 0; g <= 12; g++) { b.create('segment', [[g, 0], [g, 9]], {strokeColor: '#999999', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } for (var h = 0; h <= 9; h++) { b.create('segment', [[0, h], [12, h]], {strokeColor: '#999999', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } var X = [], Y = []; for (var k = 0; k <= poly.length; k++) { X.push(poly[k % poly.length][0]); Y.push(poly[k % poly.length][1]); } b.create('curve', [X, Y], {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 2, fillColor: '#cccccc', fillOpacity: 0, fixed: true, highlight: false}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

There are \(F = {@nF@}\) full squares and \(P = {@nP@}\) part squares. A part square is, on average, about half covered, so each part square counts as \(\tfrac{1}{2}\):

\[\text{estimate} = F + \tfrac{1}{2}P = {@nF@} + \tfrac{1}{2} \times {@nP@} = {@est@} \text{ squares}\]

One square has area \({@s@} \times {@s@} = {@sq@}\,\text{m}^2\), so the area is about \({@est@} \times {@sq@} = {@area@}\,\text{m}^2\).

Hand counts of a drawn shape can differ by a square or two, so counts within \(1\) full square and \(2\) part squares of these were accepted.

questionnote.text: ix={@ix@}, s={@s@}, F={@nF@}, P={@nP@}, est={@est@}, area={@area@}

questiondescription.text:
Area Approximations: estimating an area by counting squares

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.2 (a) / Essential 2.1 (a): Count the full and part squares of an irregular shape on a grid, estimate its area as full + half of part squares, and convert to square metres.

Core and Essential

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core and Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: Some of the squares you counted as full have the edge passing through them. Count those as part squares.
You have missed some part squares. Count every square the edge passes through, even if only a little of the shape is inside it.

falsefeedback.text: Count again: first the squares wholly inside the shape, then every square the edge passes through.
Your estimate follows correctly from your counts, but the counts in (a) and (b) are not right.

truefeedback.text: You counted each part square as a whole square. Each part square counts as half: \({@ans1@} + \tfrac{1}{2} \times {@ans2@}\).
You left out the part squares. Add half of them to the full squares.
You halved the full squares as well. Only the part squares are halved.

falsefeedback.text: Your counts are \({@ans1@}\) full squares and \({@ans2@}\) part squares. Full squares count \(1\) each and part squares \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) each, and that does not come to \({@ans3@}\).

feedbackvariables.text: okc: is(abs(ans1-nF) <= 1 and abs(ans2-nP) <= 2 and abs(ans3-(ans1+ans2/2)) < 1/1000); dok: is(abs(ans1-nF) <= 1 and abs(ans2-nP) <= 2 and abs(ans4-sq*(ans1+ans2/2)) < 1/1000);

falsefeedback.text: Your method is right for your estimate in (c), but that estimate is not right, so check (a) to (c).

truefeedback.text: You multiplied by \({@s@}\), the length of a side. One square has area \({@s@} \times {@s@} = {@sq@}\,\text{m}^2\).
That is the number of squares. Multiply it by the area of one square, \({@sq@}\,\text{m}^2\).

falsefeedback.text: One square stands for \({@s@}\,\text{m}\) by \({@s@}\,\text{m}\). Find the area of one square in square metres, then multiply it by your \({@ans3@}\) squares. That does not give \({@ans4@}\,\text{m}^2\).

node.description: Area right for own counts although (c) is not

truefeedback.text: Your area is right for your counts in (a) and (b). Your estimate in (c) does not match those counts, so check (c).
